name: Siemens Ltd.
business_summary: Indian listed arm of Siemens AG (75%). After demerging the Energy business into Siemens Energy India (2025) and selling its Low Voltage Motors business (gain Rs 2,099 cr in Q1 FY27), it operates Smart Infrastructure (electrical products, building technology, power distribution), Digital Industries (automation, drives, software) and Mobility (locomotives, metro and rail signalling). Financial year changed to March (18-month period to Mar 2026). TTM sales Rs 18,062 cr, OPM only 9-11%, large treasury (other income Rs 2,177 cr). Q1 FY27: revenue Rs 4,714 cr (+14.8%), backlog Rs 46,670 cr (+9.6%). Valuation P/E 81 reflects the one-off gain and depressed margins.

exposures.mechanism: Digital Industries (factory automation, drives) and Smart Infrastructure follow private capex. +10% capex growth -> revenue +5% (elasticity 0.5) at ~25% contribution margin vs 9-11% OPM -> EBITDA +11% to +14%; persistence 0.5; EV/MCap ~0.9 -> ~+5, haircut to 4.5.

evidence.note: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 4,714 cr +14.8%; PAT Rs 2,143 cr incl. Rs 2,099 cr one-off LVM sale gain; ex-gain PAT ~Rs 343 cr (-19%); backlog Rs 46,670 cr +9.6%

exposures.mechanism: Mobility (locomotives, metros, signalling), smart infrastructure for public projects; +10% -> revenue +3% -> EBITDA +7% -> persistence 0.5 -> ~+2.5.

Mobility is ~15% of revenue (estimate; group won 100 Vectron X locomotives in Europe 2026-09-23 but that is group-level, not SIEMENS Ltd); +10% railway capex -> mobility revenue +10% -> EBITDA +4% -> ~+2.
Smart Infrastructure (electrical products, building management, power distribution) for data centres; ~8% of demand; +1 unit -> +20% -> revenue +1.6% -> EBITDA +4% -> ~+2.5.
Factory relocation to India lifts automation spending (Digital Industries).
PLI manufacturing capex drives automation orders; small.

Copper in low/medium voltage and distribution products ~5% of costs; +10% -> cost +0.5%, 50% recovered -> EBITDA -2.5% at 10% OPM; persistence 0.25 -> -0.3. Pack shows +1.65 per +10% (t=+2.1) which reflects the capex-cycle correlation (copper rises with industrial demand), not a cost benefit; conflict noted and range spans zero.

Imports from Siemens group are a large share of Digital Industries and Mobility content (~35% of revenue, estimate); +3% -> cost +1.0% of revenue, ~40% recovered via price lists -> EBITDA hit 0.6% of revenue vs 10% OPM = -6%; persistence 0.4; EV/MCap 0.9 -> ~-2, set to -1.5. Pack: USDCNY -3.86 per +3% (t=-1.8), consistent with import/EM-currency sensitivity.
P/E 81 on depressed margin (OPM 9%) means very long duration; net cash ~Rs 7,000 cr incl. LVM proceeds. +25 bp -> ~-2.
Pack +2.04 per +5% S&P (t=+2.4): global industrial-tech/AI-electrification sentiment co-movement; shrunk for overlap with data-centre theme.

ABB India, Schneider, Hitachi Energy, Legrand and Chinese-backed competitors in electrification/automation; OPM already fell to 9%. +1 unit = 100 bp margin pressure -> EBITDA -10% at 10% OPM, persistence 0.5, probability 0.4 -> ~-2.
Parent group's European demand affects technology roadmap and component pricing; small direct effect on India revenue.
